html:
In 1860 a war broke out in Mount Lebanon between Druze and Maronite Christians. Thousands of Christians were killed in towns such as Deir el-Qamar and Zahle, and in July the violence spread to Damascus, where a mob killed thousands more.

Tension had grown for decades over land and power, as Maronite peasants rose against Druze lords and the Ottoman reforms changed old ways. In Damascus the exiled Algerian leader Emir Abdelkader sheltered thousands of Christians in his house.

France sent troops. In 1861 the European powers and the Ottomans set up the Mutasarrifate of Mount Lebanon, a self-governing district under a Christian governor. It was the first form of a Lebanese state. Many Christians emigrated after the massacres (Lebanese emigration).
sum: In 1860 a war broke out in Mount Lebanon between Druze and Maronite Christians. Thousands of Christians were killed in towns such as Deir el-Qamar and Zahle, and in July the violence spread to Damascus, where a mob killed thousands more.
